sections.title: Living things
sections.description: Telling living from non-living, what plants need to grow, and our bodies and senses.

sections.title: Materials around me
sections.description: What everyday things are made from, how materials feel, and using your senses to explore and sort them.

sections.title: Pushes, pulls and sounds
sections.description: How pushes and pulls start, speed up and stop things, and how sounds are made and heard.

questions.question: Sara sees a goat, a bicycle, a stone and a bucket. Which one is living?
questions.options: the bicycle | the goat | the bucket | the stone
questions.explanation: A goat eats, moves and grows, so it is living. The bicycle, stone and bucket cannot do any of those things.

questions.question: Which of these can ALL living things do?
questions.options: grow | melt | float | shine
questions.explanation: Every living thing grows — plants, animals and people all get bigger as they live.

questions.question: A toy car moves when you push it. Why is it still NOT living?
questions.options: It does not eat, grow or have babies | It is too small to be living | It is the wrong colour | It moves too slowly
questions.correctAnswer: It does not eat, grow or have babies
questions.explanation: Moving is not enough. Living things also eat, grow and make new living things — a toy car cannot do any of that.

questions.question: Omar plants a bean seed. Which two things must he give it so it can start to grow?
questions.options: ice and snow | sweets and milk | water and warmth | wind and dust
questions.explanation: Seeds wake up and start to grow when they have water and warmth.

questions.question: Which part of a plant drinks water from the soil?
questions.options: the petal | the leaf | the flower | the roots
questions.explanation: The roots grow down into the soil and drink up the water the plant needs.

questions.question: Layla plants two seeds in the same soil. She waters one every day and gives the other no water at all. What is she trying to find out?
questions.options: how heavy the soil is | which seed is prettier | what colour the pots are | if seeds need water to grow
questions.correctAnswer: if seeds need water to grow
questions.explanation: By changing only the water, Layla can see what water does — that is how scientists test one idea at a time.

questions.question: Which body part do you use to smell fresh bread?
questions.options: your nose | your feet | your eyes | your ears
questions.explanation: Your nose is for smelling — it tells you when fresh bread is near before you even see it.

questions.question: Hamza closes his eyes tightly. Which sense can he no longer use?
questions.options: seeing | hearing | tasting | smelling
questions.explanation: We see with our eyes, so when they are closed the sense of seeing stops — but he can still hear, smell and taste.

questions.question: Baby Idris was small last year. Now he is taller and his old shoes do not fit. What does this show?
questions.options: He is shrinking | He is non-living | He is growing | His shoes grew
questions.explanation: People are living things, and living things grow — that is why Idris got taller and needs bigger shoes.

questions.question: Which of these objects is made of metal?
questions.options: a paper book | a rubber ball | a woolly jumper | a steel spoon
questions.explanation: Steel is a metal, so a steel spoon is made of metal. Wool, paper and rubber are different materials.

questions.question: How does a rock feel when you touch it?
questions.options: wet | bendy | hard | soft
questions.explanation: A rock feels hard — it does not squash or bend when you press it.

questions.question: Why is a raincoat made of plastic and not of paper?
questions.options: Plastic keeps the rain out | Paper is stronger than plastic | Plastic smells nicer | Paper keeps you drier
questions.explanation: Plastic is waterproof, so the rain runs off it. Paper soaks up water and would fall apart in the rain.

questions.question: Nadia is making a group of things made of wood. Which object belongs in her group?
questions.options: a wooden door | a metal key | a glass cup | a woolly hat
questions.explanation: A wooden door is made of wood, so it belongs. The cup, key and hat are made of glass, metal and wool.

questions.question: A window lets you see the garden outside. Which material is the window made from?
questions.options: stone | glass | wood | wool
questions.explanation: Glass is see-through, so windows are made of glass to let us look outside.

questions.question: Bilal wants to build a strong little bridge for his toy cars. Which material is the best choice?
questions.options: cotton wool | jelly | wood | tissue paper
questions.explanation: Wood is hard and stiff, so it can hold the toy cars up. Tissue paper, cotton wool and jelly are too soft and weak.

questions.question: Zahra feels a mystery object inside a bag without looking at it. Which sense is she using to explore it?
questions.options: hearing | touch | sight | taste
questions.explanation: Her hands feel if the object is hard, soft, smooth or rough — that is the sense of touch, and it helps scientists explore materials.

questions.question: Which sense tells you that a lemon is sour?
questions.options: touch | hearing | sight | taste
questions.explanation: Your tongue tastes the lemon — taste is the sense that tells you if food is sour, sweet or salty.

questions.question: Kicking a football away from you is a...
questions.options: sound | smell | pull | push
questions.explanation: When your foot sends the ball away from you, that force is a push.

questions.question: Musa gives his toy car a bigger push than before. What happens to the car?
questions.options: It moves faster and goes farther | It rolls backwards | It stops at once | It gets heavier
questions.correctAnswer: It moves faster and goes farther
questions.explanation: A bigger push is a bigger force, so the car moves faster and travels farther before it stops.

questions.question: Which of these is a pull?
questions.options: pushing a swing forward | opening a drawer towards you | pressing a doorbell | kicking a ball away
questions.explanation: A pull moves something towards you — like sliding a drawer out. The others all push things away.

questions.question: A ball is rolling towards Maryam and she wants to stop it. What should she do?
questions.options: Put her hands in its path and push against it | Walk away from the ball | Shout at the ball loudly | Close her eyes and wait
questions.correctAnswer: Put her hands in its path and push against it
questions.explanation: A force can stop a moving thing. When Maryam's hands push against the rolling ball, it slows down and stops.

questions.question: Dawud hears the school bell ring. Which body part is he using?
questions.options: his ears | his eyes | his nose | his hands
questions.explanation: Sounds travel to our ears — that is how Dawud hears the bell.

questions.question: Halima taps a drum and the drum skin shakes very fast, making a sound. What is this fast shaking called?
questions.options: a reflection | a melt | a shadow | a vibration
questions.explanation: The fast shaking that makes a sound is called a vibration — every sound starts with one.

questions.question: Which of these makes a quiet sound?
questions.options: a drum bang | a fire engine siren | a clap of thunder | a whisper
questions.explanation: A whisper is soft and quiet. Drums, sirens and thunder all make loud sounds.

questions.question: Adam walks away from a ringing bell. What happens to the sound he hears?
questions.options: It turns into light | It stays exactly the same | It gets louder | It gets quieter
questions.explanation: The farther you are from a sound, the quieter it seems — so as Adam walks away, the bell sounds quieter and quieter.
